correctness.rationale: The tangent- and chord-line distance formulas make the deficit affine in P, so vertex checking is sufficient. At a vertex, setting y_j=sin x_j gives exact identities sum D=2 sum y_j^2 and sum d=2 sum y_j y_{j+1}. The sharp Dirichlet path eigenvalue is cos(pi/n), proving the inequality. The equality eigenspace yields equal adjacent half-gap sines; cycling plus sum alpha_i=pi forces every half-gap to pi/n, hence regularity. The actual verifier checks the coordinate identities, path inequality, main inequality, and regular equality on nonuniform cyclic polygons through n=15; the proof itself is exact.

final_claim: For a convex cyclic \(n\)-gon with no consecutive antipodal vertices and an interior point \(P\), \(\sum_iD_i\ge\sec(\pi/n)\sum_id_i\); the constant is sharp, with interior equality exactly for regular cyclic polygons.
limitations: Euclidean convex cyclic polygons only; consecutive antipodal vertices are excluded.
No nonconvex, exterior-point, or non-Euclidean extension is claimed.
